bounds: One sign-in at clock 0, three credential identities, two renewal requests, clock 0..6, cap 2, credential lifetime 3 and code lifetime 1. A third renewal and a second sign-in are outside the instance.
fairness: An authorized renewal settles under weak fairness of its issuing transaction. Starting a renewal, redeeming a code and revoking the predecessor are not promised.
limitations: One sign-in at clock 0, three credential identities, two renewal requests, clock 0..6, cap 2, credential lifetime 3 and code lifetime 1. A third renewal and a second sign-in are outside the instance.
Exchange and acknowledgement of a renewal code are one atomic redemption. MobileAppCredential models them for one code. Composition is not mechanically established.

Owner eligibility groups the inactive user, changed organization and closed or deletion-fenced organization into one flag, and client availability groups the registry entry and the app row. Both only ever turn off.
The 401, 403, 409, 429 and 503 answers are one refusal outcome. Limiter buckets, request bodies, PKCE bytes and secret hashes are not modeled.
A grant issued before the session_started_at column counts from created_at. The model starts every lineage at the sign-in time.
The predecessor stays valid until the phone revokes it or it expires. Revocation by the phone is not promised.

assumptions: Checked formula in MobileAppKeyRenewal: RequestsSettle = Fairness implies eventually(always(Idle))
Model fairness predicate Fairness = Requests.forall(r => CommitRenew(r).weakFair(s))
The property is conditional on its written model fairness and environmental premises. Real scheduler fairness, database completion and implementation refinement are not proved.
